topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Drivers of Cancer Risk: Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer etiology by examining how intrinsic mutational processes, environmental exposures, and epidemiological variations influence cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens drive carcinogenesis, highlighting the mechanism and cofactors involved in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenic Carcinogens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation and chemical agents cause DNA damage directly or through host metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic mechanisms such as chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and host developmental timing enable neoplastic outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, and laboratory approaches used to prove carcinogenicity and evaluate exposure risks.
